abstract:
Understanding the biological functions and regulatory mechanisms that shape cancer outcomes is critical for explaining cancer progression and guiding targeted therapies. Integrative analysis of multi-omics data has become widely used to provide a more complete molecular view of cancer. However, many phenotype changes driven by protein abnormalities arise from upstream regulatory processes, and existing methods often ignore transcript variants generated by post-transcriptional events such as alternative splicing and alternative polyadenylation. To address this limitation, we propose Pathway-Transformer, a computational framework that integrates transcript variants and gene expression derived from the same RNA-seq data to predict cancer phenotypes using biological pathways as prior knowledge. Pathway-Transformer encodes the structural properties of pathway networks and uses a transformer encoder to learn pathway-specific representations of transcriptional regulation, which are then aggregated across pathways for phenotype prediction.
We evaluate Pathway-Transformer on TCGA breast cancer patient samples using multiple cancer-related KEGG pathways. Results from both individual pathways and integrated pathway sets consistently show that transcript variants derived from alternative splicing and alternative polyadenylation provide more informative molecular signatures and lead to improved clinical outcome prediction compared with gene expression profiles alone. Applying the same experimental setup to the METABRIC breast cancer cohort yields comparable performance for cancer status prediction, indicating that the framework is not specific to a single cohort. In addition, analysis of the highest performing pathways and of attention scores computed from the learned parameters identified biologically relevant hormone receptor and signaling programs, supporting the interpretability of the proposed framework.
Source code is available at: https://github.com/compbiolabucf/PathwayTransformer.
